text:
alex: FYI — AcmeBooks reported a batch of card declines that all fail right after the 3DS step. Acquirer note: `3DS_DEVICE_FINGERPRINT_MISMATCH`. Affected txns: t_1801, t_1802, t_1803. Seeing `do_not_honor` at the gateway. Can we triage?

julia: Thanks — do we have the raw gateway responses and the Redwood API request for one of the txns? Also what platform (web/mobile)?

alex: Web checkout, React app inside an embedded webview for their mobile PWA. Pasted a sanitized log for t_1801: 
```
POST /v1/charges
{ "merchant_id": "m_88", "amount": 1299, "card": {"last4": "4242"}, "three_ds": true, "return_url": "https://acmebooks.com/3ds-callback" }
Response: 402 Declined
gateway_code: do_not_honor
acquirer_note: 3DS_DEVICE_FINGERPRINT_MISMATCH
ds_trans_id: dstr_9a7b
eci: 05
acs_url: https://acs.example-issuer/pareq
```

tyler: ECI 05 means SCA attempted but auth failed. Device fingerprint mismatch typically means the device/browser fingerprint the DS has is different from what the merchant sent to the DS during authentication. Common causes: CSP blocking fingerprint script, webview not forwarding headers, or double-redirect breaking session.

alex: Merchant claims they did nothing different; they just updated a CDN rule around the same time. Could CSP be stripping the 3DS script?

julia: Possible. Can you ask the merchant to check that: 1) our 3DS JS (dsf.js) loads successfully (200) on the page where they initiate auth, 2) no `X-Frame-Options`/CSP frame-ancestors blocking the ACS iframe, and 3) cookies/storage are available in the webview.

alex: I ran a quick curl to the checkout page and dsf.js returns 200. But when I simulate via a headless WebView (`wkwebview`), the script is blocked with the console: `Refused to execute inline script because of CSP` — so likely fingerprint couldn't run.

payments-bot: Automated check completed for merchant m_88: ds_js_load: FAILED in embedded-webview scenario; acquirer reported 3 failures in last 30m. Suggested action: ask merchant to allow dsf.js and ensure storage is available.

tyler: If merchant can't relax CSP, workaround is to use server-assisted device fingerprinting or fallback to a different SCA flow (redirect/OTP) — but acquirer support needed. We should also check if our SDK has an option to use iframe-based fallback.

julia: For support ticket: collect one full exchange (merchant request -> Redwood -> DS -> ACS response) with headers `User-Agent`, `Referer`, `Origin`, and the DS client script load logs. Also ask merchant to try in a normal mobile browser (not embedded) and confirm whether 3DS succeeds. That'll help isolate webview vs acquirer.

alex: I'll request the headers + a repro video and ask them to test in Chrome on Android. Also opened acquirer case with reference `ACQ-7132` asking if they can provide more detail on the fingerprint mismatch.

tyler: If acquirer confirms mismatch is due to changed device fingerprint, we'll mark this as `action: merchant CSM` — they need to relax CSP or change integration. If it's on our side (e.g., we altered the ds request headers recently), escalate to eng-payments.

alex: Quick status update — merchant tried in Chrome (non-webview) and 3DS passed for the same card. So reproducible only in their PWA webview. I've flagged the CSM and set next step: ask their mobile team to enable third-party cookies/session storage for the webview and allow `dsf.js`.

julia: Sounds good. Keep thread updated. If merchant reports it's still failing after webview fix, capture a HAR from the failing flow and paste here. :thumbsup:
